subject: Agriculture
title: Perennial Grains
description: A short lesson to help you apply Perennial Grains.

hook.text: What if wheat didn't need replanting every year? Perennial grains could end annual tillage forever.

buildup.text: Annual crops require plowing, seeding, and establishment every season—exposing soil to erosion each time.

discovery.text: Kernza, a perennial wheat relative, regrows from its roots for 3–5 years. No replanting, no tillage.

twist.text: Perennial roots grow 3 meters deep—holding soil, storing carbon, and accessing water annuals can't reach.

climax.text: Kernza yields are still only 25% of annual wheat. Decades of breeding lie ahead before it competes.

punchline.text: A grain you plant once and harvest for years. It exists—it just needs work.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of perennial grains like Kernza?
options: They regrow from roots without annual replanting, preventing erosion

details.summary: Perennial grains are crops that regrow after harvest without replanting, unlike annuals that must be sown each year. This topic covers Kernza and other perennial grain research, their deep root systems, and the environmental benefits of permanent crop cover.
details.whyItMatters: Annual grain farming requires yearly tillage that erodes soil, releases carbon, and consumes energy. Perennial grains could transform agriculture by maintaining year-round root systems that protect and build soil.
takeaways: Kernza, a perennial wheatgrass, is the most advanced perennial grain in development
Perennial root systems can reach 3 meters deep, sequestering carbon and preventing erosion
Perennial grains eliminate annual planting costs and reduce soil disturbance dramatically

faq.question: What are perennial grains and how do they differ from annual crops?
faq.answer: Perennial grains regrow from their root systems after harvest, producing grain for multiple years without replanting. Annual grains like wheat and corn die after each season and must be replanted, requiring repeated tillage and seed.

faq.question: What is Kernza and where is it being grown?
faq.answer: Kernza is a perennial wheatgrass developed by The Land Institute. It produces grain similar to wheat and is now grown commercially in the upper Midwest US, used in bread, beer, and pasta, with acreage expanding as yields improve through breeding.
